text: Confirmed: in gin's errors.go, `Error()` has a value receiver but `Unwrap()` has a pointer receiver, so a `gin.Error` value implements `error` without an `Unwrap` method — errors.Is/As can't see through it (the pointer form works). Fixing it now; ETA ~5 min.

Fixed. In errors.go, `Unwrap()` had a pointer receiver while `Error()` has a value receiver, so a `gin.Error` value satisfied `error` but had no `Unwrap` method — errors.Is/As couldn't see through it. Changed `func (msg *Error) Unwrap() error` to a value receiver `func (msg Error) Unwrap() error`, so both the value and pointer forms now interoperate with errors.Is/As/Unwrap. Verified with a standalone program (value form: errors.Is=true, errors.As=true; pointer form unchanged) and `go test ./...` passes with no regressions.

Confirmed: responseWriter.WriteHeader logs the "headers were already written" warning but then still assigns w.status = code, so Status() reports a code that was never sent. It should return early once the response is written. Fixing now; ETA ~6 min.

Fixed. In response_writer.go, WriteHeader now returns early after the "headers were already written" warning instead of still assigning w.status = code, so Status() keeps the status that was actually sent (200 in your example). Verified: the late WriteHeader(401) leaves Status()==200 and the client receives 200; the normal pre-write path (e.g. WriteHeader(301) before writing) is unchanged; full `go test ./... -count=1` passes with identical results to the baseline (416 PASS, 0 FAIL).

Confirmed the cause: contexts are pooled and their param slice is sized from engine.maxParams at allocation time, while maxParams only grows when a route is added. A context allocated before your param route existed keeps a zero-capacity params slice, and tree.go's getValue silently drops `:param` values when `cap(*params) == 0` (the catch-all branch can even panic). Fixing so per-request capacity is guaranteed / params are grown safely. ETA ~10 min.

Confirmed: in tree.go's findCaseInsensitivePathRec, when a node has a wildcard child the code assumes the wildcard is children[0], but gin keeps it last — so it walks into a static node whose nType is 0 and panics with "invalid node type". Fixing it to try static children case-insensitively first (so /PREFIX/XXX redirects to /prefix/xxx) and fall back to the wildcard child (/prefix/a/b/c → 404). ETA ~12 min.

Confirmed: NegotiateFormat's inner loop indexes offer[i] with i bounded by len(accepted), so a longer Accept entry ("image/tiff-fx" vs offer "image/tiff") reads past the end and panics. Fixing it to bound the comparison by both lengths and only match when the accepted value is a prefix of the offer. ETA ~8 min.

Confirmed: FileAttachment embeds the filename in `attachment; filename="..."` without escaping, so quotes/backslashes pass through and inject extra header parameters. Fixing it to escape `\` and `"` in the ASCII branch (non-ASCII keeps filename*=UTF-8''). ETA ~8 min.

Fixed. FileAttachment now escapes `\` and `"` in the filename before writing the ASCII form, so `evil"; dummy="x.sh` becomes `attachment; filename="evil\"; dummy=\"x.sh"` — one well-formed filename parameter (verified with mime.ParseMediaType). Plain filenames are unchanged and non-ASCII still uses filename*=UTF-8''. Full test suite passes with no regressions.

Fixed. NegotiateFormat now bounds the comparison by both the accepted value and the offer, and only returns an offer when the accepted value is a prefix of it — so "image/tiff-fx" vs offer "image/tiff" returns "" instead of panicking. Wildcard ('*') behavior is unchanged, and the full test suite passes with no regressions.
